evidence_summary: Höfner's 1967 catalog introduced the No. 540 Fuzz Tone, and the vintage Höfner archive notes that the same pedals were also available with Schaller markings; the archive therefore treats Schaller as the physical-builder attribution while retaining Höfner as the marketed identity.

Effects Database identifies the Höfner No. 539 as a rare 1960s OEM pedal built by Schaller in West Germany and related directly to the Schaller Fuzz; Höfner's own archive separately documents the No. 539 as a later catalog distortion device.
Effects Database documents the Höfner Wha-Wha-Fuzz as a Schaller-produced West German pedal and identifies the closely related Schaller Wha-Wha-Fuzz and Kent 6406 states.
Effects Database documents the Schaller Fuzz-Sustain as designed and manufactured by Schaller and distributed under Höfner Fuzz-Sustain and Allsound SC-30/SC-31 identities.

Effects Database states that the Höfner Double Pedal is a German late-1960s unit built in collaboration with or directly rebranded from Schaller's Universalfußpedal; the Schaller version is separately cataloged as the physical reference state.
Effects Database identifies the Kent 6400 as an OEM-branded version of the Schaller Fuzz produced in West Germany; surviving period listings also identify it as a rebranded Schaller unit.
Effects Database identifies the Blackfield Fuzz as an OEM version of the Schaller Fuzz made in West Germany, retaining Blackfield as the marketed identity.
Van Hall is consistently listed among related Schaller Fuzz identities, but current evidence reviewed here does not provide model-specific builder proof strong enough to move beyond candidate status.

The vintage Höfner archive confirms a West German Höfner wah/fuzz line and notes substantial Schaller involvement across the pedal range, but it also flags uncertainty around individual early models and possible Vox-derived enclosure influence; no blanket Schaller attribution is made here.
